lessons.title: What are Wh Questions?
lessons.content: There are two types of questions in English: Wh-questions and Yes/No questions. Wh-questions are open questions that require specific information as an answer, unlike Yes/No questions which can be answered with a simple 'Yes' or 'No'.

details.description: Questions that can be answered with Yes or No
details.answer_type: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
details.burmese: မင်း ကော်ဖီ ကြိုက်လား။ ဟုတ်/မဟုတ်

details.description: Open questions that require specific information
details.burmese: မင်း ဘာ ကြိုက်တာလဲ။ အသေးစိတ် အဖြေ လိုတယ်

lessons.title: Asking About People (Who, Whom, Whose)
lessons.content: We use 'Who' to ask about people as the subject, 'Whom' to ask about people as the object, and 'Whose' to ask about possession.

details.burmese: သူမက ဘယ်သူလဲ။
details.note: When 'who' is the subject, no auxiliary is needed: Who likes soccer?

details.burmese: မင်း ဘယ်သူ့ကို တွေ့တာလဲ။
details.note: Whom is more formal. In everyday speech, 'who' is often used instead.

details.burmese: ဒီစာအုပ်က ဘယ်သူ့ဟာလဲ။
details.note: Whose is always followed by a noun.

lessons.title: Asking About Things and Time (What, When, Which)
lessons.content: We use 'What' to ask about things or information, 'When' to ask about time, and 'Which' to ask about choices from a limited set.

details.usage: To ask about something or information
details.burmese: ဒီနေ့က ဘယ်နေ့လဲ။
details.note: What can be used with nouns: What time, What day, What color

details.burmese: မင်း မွေးနေ့က ဘယ်အချိန်လဲ။
details.note: When asks about a specific time or period

details.usage: To ask about choices from a limited set
details.structure: Which + noun + auxiliary + subject + main verb?
details.example: Which restaurant shall we go to?
details.burmese: ငါတို့ ဘယ်စားသောက်ဆိုင် သွားရမလဲ။
details.note: Which is used when there are limited options to choose from

lessons.title: Asking About Place and Reason (Where, Why)
lessons.content: We use 'Where' to ask about place or location, and 'Why' to ask about the reason or purpose.

details.usage: To ask about place or location
details.burmese: မင်း ဘယ်မှာ အလုပ်လုပ်တာလဲ။
details.note: Where can be used with be verbs: Where is my pencil case?
Why questions often begin with 'Because' in the answer

lessons.title: Asking About Manner and Quantity (How)
lessons.content: We use 'How' to ask about manner, condition, or degree. 'How' can combine with adjectives and adverbs to ask about specific quantities or qualities.

details.usage: To ask about manner or condition
details.burmese: ဒါက ဘယ်လို အလုပ်လုပ်တာလဲ။
details.note: How alone asks about manner or way

details.structure: How many + plural noun + auxiliary + subject + verb?
details.burmese: ဘေးပင် ဘယ်နှစ်ချောင်း ရှိလဲ။
details.note: How many is used with countable nouns

details.usage: To ask about uncountable quantity or price
details.structure: How much + uncountable noun + auxiliary + subject + verb?
details.example: How much money do you have?
details.burmese: မင်းမှာ ဘယ်လောက် ငွေရှိလဲ။
details.note: How much is used with uncountable nouns

details.burmese: မင်း အသက် ဘယ်နှစ်လဲ။
details.note: How old specifically asks about someone's age

details.burmese: စားသောက်ဆိုင်က ဘယ်လောက် ဝေးလဲ။
details.note: How far asks about the distance between two places

details.usage: To ask about duration or length
details.burmese: ဘယ်လောက် ကြာမလဲ။
details.note: How long asks about time duration or physical length
